description:
Workspace AGENTS.md 'Caller identity (foundation seam)' establishes JmapBackend::principal_id(caller) -> Option<&Id> as the canonical (and only) way for a method to learn who is asking. ContactsBackend (backend.rs:34-111) extends JmapBackend, so technically it inherits the seam. But:

 1. No method in handle_address_book_* or handle_contact_card_* calls principal_id.
 2. No test exercises principal_id.
 3. No doc comment on ContactsBackend explains how the seam relates to contacts (AddressBook ACLs, shareWith write authorization, isSubscribed-per-user state).

The crate-level AGENTS.md DOES include the 'Permission enforcement: backend canonical' section that says 'every AddressBook / ContactCard mutation must be authorized against the caller's effective rights on the AddressBook (RFC 9670 myRights semantics, propagated through jmap-sharing-server when present)'. So the intent is documented in agents, but not in the public type or in any reachable code path. Contributors searching for principal_id usage in this crate will find zero hits and conclude that contacts doesn't use the seam.

The proximate maintainer-burden cost is: a future contributor will add per-user-AddressBook-rights enforcement and won't know whether it goes in handler or backend. The workspace rule says backend; the contacts-server crate has no exemplary code showing what that looks like. Cross-reference: the jmap-chat-server canonical Space/set permission-enforcement work (JMAP-g7wu.2.4) is the first consumer of the seam; that pattern needs to be mirrored here.

Lower-priority because no code uses it yet, so there's no regression risk to fix; but raising it as 'risk' because the gap will calcify if AddressBook ACL enforcement work doesn't engage with the seam at the same time.
title: ContactsBackend trait has no fn principal_id — does not engage the workspace caller-identity foundation seam
